premises.text: Home restaurants, underground dining, and pop-ups worldwide show a durable human need to share authentic food with others
premises.evidence_span: this basic human need to share food with others existed in the past, it exists in the present, and it will continue to exist in the future

premises.text: EatWith is a community marketplace that wraps business structure, safety, and trust around authentic home dining and makes it bookable worldwide
premises.evidence_span: simply put business structure, safety, and trust around this phenomena and make it accessible to tens of millions more around the world

premises.text: Verified hosts, a $1 million guarantee, ratings/reviews, and secure online payment including commission make bookings safe and simple
premises.evidence_span: Joel is an Eat With verified host, which means that all of his events are protected under the Eat With $1 million guarantee

premises.text: Hosts can pursue cooking passion and meet people while earning extra income
premises.evidence_span: Eat With lets me do this while earning some extra income

premises.text: Demand comes from tourists seeking authentic local meals and from locals booking parties, classes, and social events
premises.evidence_span: 50% of all our booking during our pilot came from locals

value.text: Travelers and locals get great food, interesting people, and unforgettable authentic dining experiences
value.evidence_span: we want great food, interesting people, and unforgettable experiences

secondary_value.text: Hosts earn extra income from their passion for cooking and meeting people

causal_links.evidence_span: basic human need to share food with others
community marketplace for authentic dining experiences
Creating new dishes, meeting new people
Most of the tourists want to meet the locals and to have an authentic dining experience

notes: Verified host, guarantee, ratings, and payment/commission folded as trust-and-booking package of the marketplace (§4.1.7–8). Restaurant-industry TAM framing excluded. Pilot city expansion treated as launch announcement, not a premise. Four-domain partition; not a need/product/money triad.
